children: opened about 10% higher after J.P. Morgan initiated coverage of the stock with an overweight rating and a December 2027 price target of $8.
Current PT represents about 40% upside from its last close.

stands out for a "scarce mix" of above-market growth, earnings visibility, and improving profitability, despite a challenging backdrop for online sports betting and concerns surrounding its $1.2 billion Legend acquisition.
J.P. Morgan forecasts pro forma revenue growth of 18% annually from fiscal 2026 through 2028, with about 42% EBITDA flow-through. It said Genius
trades at roughly 5x and 4x fiscal 2027/28 estimated EV/EBITDA, about a 1x discount to peer Sportradar, despite a higher growth outlook.

Hirsh also sees upside from prediction markets, estimating a potential $30 million-$35 million of incremental EBITDA at maturity, while saying estimates already sit 3%-4% below Genius’ Investor Day targets, limiting downside if sports prediction markets face regulatory restrictions.
The analysts said "Legend execution" could be a catalyst, with early performance showing faster-than-expected synergies and active cross-selling.
Key risks include sports-rights renewals, prediction-market regulation, AI and affiliate disruption, a sustained sports-betting slowdown, and Legend integration.

title: Genius Sports rallies after JPMorgan initiates at overweight with $8 PT
